links.outcome: Model discrimination across five hospitals in two countries and age subgroups
links.effect: AUROC 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.82) for under-5 but 0.62 (0.55-0.70) for neonates; revised neonatal model AUROC 0.83 (0.79-0.87)
links.quote: The model achieved good discrimination for children under-5 with AUROC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.82) but poor discrimination for neonates with AUROC of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.55-0.70).

links.outcome: Neonatal model discrimination after re-estimating intercept, coefficients and thresholds locally
links.effect: Neonate AUROC improved from 0.62 to 0.83 (0.79-0.87) with 13% and 41% low- and high-risk thresholds
links.quote: After model revision for neonates, we achieved an AUROC of 0.83 (0.79-0.87) with 13% and 41% as the low- and high-risk thresholds, respectively.

links.outcome: Model performance in neonatal subgroup beyond original target population
links.effect: Neonates had poor discrimination (AUROC 0.62, 95% CI 0.55-0.70) and low-risk threshold sensitivity of 0.68 versus 0.85 for under-5
links.quote: However, a revised model is recommended for neonates due to their uniqueness in disease susceptibly, host response, and underlying physiological reserve.

links.outcome: Performance across age subgroups compared to aggregate
links.effect: Aggregate under-5 AUROC 0.81 masked poor neonatal AUROC 0.62; sensitivity at low-risk threshold 0.85 vs 0.68
links.quote: Sensitivity at the low-risk thresholds (CI) were 0.85 (0.83-0.87) and 0.68 (0.58-0.76) for children under-5 and neonates, respectively.

screen.practice: local external validation and recalibration/threshold revision before deployment
screen.reason: The study conducts external geographical and subgroup validation of an existing clinical risk model (Smart Triage) across hospitals in Kenya and Uganda, demonstrating failure in neonates and evaluating model recalibration/updating and threshold re-selection.
